description: Earlier 62-card plan, preserved before consolidation into 18 substantial tasks. Not the current execution plan.

registry.status: CORE-01 reframed as a small observable capability. The other 61 cards and prerequisite links retain earlier implementation assumptions and need behavioral refinement. Implementation has not started.

tasks.title: Add a declared public capability to the connected project
tasks.hypothesis: An author can add a public capability in .expec and receive its stub in the connected project while keeping existing implementation work.
tests: With StoreGame already implemented in a connected TypeScript project, declare a new public pause() capability; building adds a public pause(): void stub that explicitly reports not implemented.
The existing startup body, private fields, helpers, and unrelated files remain unchanged.
Build the same specification again; no duplicate capability or additional edits appear.
retainedScopeForLaterRefinement: Represent a type, interface, and component.
Distinguish a dependency from an ordered interaction.
Distinguish a declaration from a reference.

tasks.title: Define scope, imports, and file-composition rules
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit visibility and attachment rules let authors split files without changing meaning.
tests: Inline and separate examples resolve equivalently.
Duplicate or ambiguous declarations have a defined outcome.
Document permitted and invalid cycles.
Define visibility for concept-local types and their use in public signatures.

tasks.title: Define the initial type system
tasks.hypothesis: Agreed type rules can catch invalid contracts while accommodating intentionally incomplete descriptions.
tests: Decide primitive, generic, literal, and concept-local types using Pair, URL, and os: windows.
Distinguish a missing type from an unfinished implementation.
Define input and output compatibility.

tasks.title: Define scenario, observation, and interaction semantics
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit behavior rules can connect inputs, state, actions, observations, and message order without interpreting prose as code.
tests: Describe the Dune scenario and an input/output example.
Distinguish an observed value from a prose promise.
Define passing results between steps and explicit message order.

tasks.title: Define the first grammar and syntax examples
tasks.hypothesis: A small, explicit grammar can express the first contracts while leaving room for broader specifications.
tests: Parse representative contracts and expectations on paper.
Distinguish literal values from names.
Identify malformed or ambiguous examples.

tasks.title: Define the manifest and dependency-resolution rules
tasks.hypothesis: One manifest can identify source inputs, project destination, targets, and dependencies without conflating their roles.
tests: Distinguish concept packages from target tooling such as Vite.
Define path and version interpretation.
Specify missing and conflicting dependency behavior.

tasks.title: Define the shared resolved-model contract
tasks.hypothesis: Exporters can share meaning without sharing a target language's syntax.
tests: Represent types, capabilities, relationships, communications, and expectations.
Retain source provenance and declaration identity.
Identify unsupported model features explicitly.

tasks.title: Define specification identity and change-ownership rules
tasks.hypothesis: An explicit identity and ownership policy can distinguish a structural edit from an accidental replacement of handwritten work.
tests: Describe identity through a rename and source-file move.
Define how existing handwritten code is associated and retained.
Specify ambiguous matches, manual edits, and deletion conflicts.

tasks.title: Define the shared output API and result contracts
tasks.hypothesis: One configured output interface can represent creation, changes, complete reads, and project-wide searches across different targets.
tests: Exercise create, insert, update, read, search, and delete with their agreed responsibilities.
Supply target options and a live project-context service once, without repeating them on each operation.
Report unsupported operations or missing information explicitly.

tasks.title: Create the seed compiler package and invocation shell
tasks.hypothesis: Authors and future test drivers can invoke a small compiler consistently before its internals are complete.
tests: Start it in a clean fixture environment.
Report malformed invocation clearly.
Report unfinished operations honestly without changing project files.

tasks.title: Implement source loading and source-location tracking
tasks.hypothesis: Every loaded construct can retain an accurate origin across multiple files.
tests: Read a multi-file fixture.
Locate text correctly with different line endings.
Report a missing source file without modifying it.

tasks.title: Implement structured diagnostics and readable reporting
tasks.hypothesis: Authors can act on compiler failures using the reported name, location, and explanation.
tests: Report errors in an included file.
Retain multiple independent diagnostics.
Distinguish failure from incomplete implementation obligations.

tasks.title: Build the independent acceptance harness
tasks.hypothesis: A small driver can exercise the real compiler and inspect diagnostics and file changes before generated tests exist.
tests: Run one valid and one invalid fixture through the real entry point.
Inspect actual project files instead of returning expected answers.
Make a deliberately incorrect validator fail the error example.

tasks.title: Implement the lexer and parser for the agreed grammar
tasks.hypothesis: The parser can preserve the written specification's structure without guessing intended syntax.
tests: Parse the approved contract corpus.
Preserve literal and prose expectations and source spans.
Reject malformed syntax at the relevant location.

tasks.title: Implement manifest loading and validation
tasks.hypothesis: Loading the manifest can give each build its project connection, targets, dependencies, version, and settings.
tests: Read the supported fields from the example manifest.
Report malformed or missing required configuration before project changes.
Resolve source and project paths using the documented path rule.

tasks.title: Implement package resolution and the resolved dependency graph
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit package resolution can supply declared dependencies reproducibly without inventing unavailable names.
tests: Resolve the supported local and package-source forms.
Diagnose missing or incompatible dependencies.
Repeat resolution against the same pinned inputs.

tasks.title: Implement module loading and declaration collection
tasks.hypothesis: Source organization can change while the compiler collects the same declarations.
tests: Load repeated references without duplicate identities.
Collect permitted mutually referring declarations.
Diagnose conflicting definitions.

tasks.title: Implement scoped name resolution
tasks.hypothesis: Every reference can resolve to an available declaration or produce a specific failure.
tests: Resolve local and imported names.
Reject saveGame when only save exists.
Reject ambiguous names without selecting an arbitrary declaration.

tasks.title: Create the declared core-type module
tasks.hypothesis: Standard types can be supplied explicitly rather than recognized through undocumented name magic.
tests: Load the agreed primitive and generic declarations.
Resolve their uses through configured availability.
Reject an unavailable core type.

tasks.title: Implement type checking for the agreed contracts
tasks.hypothesis: Type checking can validate inputs, outputs, fields, and expressions independently of implementation bodies.
tests: Accept the reviewed valid contracts.
Reject incompatible literals or incorrect generic arguments.
Validate declared contracts whose bodies remain unfinished.

tasks.title: Implement behavior-expression and composition validation
tasks.hypothesis: Checking typed scenario steps and composed operations before export will catch missing data flow and invalid expectations.
tests: Resolve and type-check actions, observations, and comparisons.
Check arguments and results passed between steps.
Reject an invalid composition cycle or unsupported predicate.

tasks.title: Implement construction and validation of the resolved model
tasks.hypothesis: Resolved declarations can become one consistent, traceable input for all exporters.
tests: Preserve shared-type identity across files.
Retain contracts, relationships, communications, and expectations.
Retain original source locations for exporter diagnostics.

tasks.title: Assemble the compiler validation pipeline
tasks.hypothesis: One validation pipeline can check all source declarations and return a resolved model without changing project files.
tests: Run source loading, parsing, resolution, and type checking through one entry point.
Reject invalid input with useful diagnostics.
Validate the supported self-description without claiming its implementation exists.

tasks.title: Implement output discovery and manifest-based target selection
tasks.hypothesis: Registered output implementations let authors choose targets without changing language interpretation.
tests: Select one or several targets from the manifest.
Add an output implementation without changing the parser.
Reject an unavailable output or incompatible configuration.

tasks.title: Connect an existing software project
tasks.hypothesis: Resolving the manifest's project connection can direct builds into an existing project without recreating it.
tests: Connect two different fixture destinations through their manifests.
Preserve existing source and unrelated files when connecting.
Report an unavailable destination without selecting another directory.

tasks.title: Implement live project context
tasks.hypothesis: A reusable context service can expose current project content to already-configured outputs.
tests: Observe edited files without reconstructing the output instance.
Discover newly added and removed project files.
Report files unavailable for inspection.

tasks.title: Implement TypeScript source inspection and edit support
tasks.hypothesis: A target-aware source adapter can locate TypeScript structures and edit their contracts while preserving implementation text.
tests: Inspect single-file and split-file Store Game implementations.
Change a signature while retaining bodies, comments, and exports.
Report unsupported syntax instead of replacing the whole file.

tasks.title: Associate specification identities with existing code
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit associations can identify existing concept implementations without depending solely on spelling or file location.
tests: Associate a concept with its source and related artifacts across files.
Distinguish two unrelated symbols with the same name.
Report ambiguous adoption instead of guessing an association.

tasks.title: Implement complete concept reads
tasks.hypothesis: read(SpecIdentifier) can retrieve the concept's complete current representation through its project associations.
tests: Return full bodies, private state, helpers, and comments in a single-file implementation.
Include every associated source and test artifact in a multi-file implementation.
Return new handwritten edits while leaving all content unchanged.

tasks.title: Implement definition and reference search
tasks.hypothesis: Target-aware search can discover actual definitions, uses, incoming consumers, and outgoing dependencies beyond the authored specification.
tests: Find aliased references and project-only consumers.
Distinguish semantic references from unrelated namesakes and comments.
Report unsupported or unavailable inspection coverage without claiming exhaustive results.

tasks.title: Implement intended-versus-actual relationship comparison
tasks.hypothesis: Comparing resolved relationships with live search results can make specification drift visible without modifying either side.
tests: For expected a,b,c and actual a,b,d, report matched a,b, missing c, and project-only d.
Do not claim absence when inspection coverage is incomplete.
Preserve project-only code and keep missing specification declarations unresolved.

tasks.title: Implement structural diffs and generation baselines
tasks.hypothesis: Comparing valid specification versions with their established output associations can identify structural changes separately from handwritten implementation changes.
tests: Identify added, changed, removed, and unchanged declarations.
Recognize a rename only when its correspondence is established.
Keep manifest version separate from the previously applied generation state.

tasks.title: Implement the TypeScript contract and stub renderer
tasks.hypothesis: The resolved model can produce TypeScript types, interfaces, classes, and public signatures with explicit unfinished bodies.
tests: Render the agreed types, contracts, and dependency imports.
Produce parseable scaffolds with explicit not-implemented methods.
Report unsupported target mappings.
Render a concept-local type used by a public signature under the chosen visibility rule.

tasks.title: Implement target setup and dependency planning
tasks.hypothesis: Target adapters can translate configured dependencies and settings into project setup changes.
tests: Produce setup changes for the first supported target.
Preserve unrelated package settings and dependency entries.
Report an unavailable target or dependency mapping.

tasks.title: Implement project initialization choice
tasks.hypothesis: An initialization flow can create and connect a project when the author chooses to start one.
tests: Offer initialization when no project is connected.
Accept the choice and create the selected target's starter project.
Decline and leave the filesystem unchanged.

tasks.title: Coordinate project mutations and detect conflicts
tasks.hypothesis: Coordinating output changes against current source can prevent stale or conflicting edits from discarding handwritten work.
tests: Detect a handwritten edit made after changes were prepared.
Report overlapping edits from multiple outputs.
On an interrupted application, retain handwritten content and report the actual partial state without claiming success.

tasks.title: Implement create and insert into connected source
tasks.hypothesis: create and insert can add generated structure directly to new or existing project files while preserving existing implementations.
tests: Create the first resolved concept and apply its target setup plan.
Insert a new capability with an explicit not-implemented stub.
Preserve existing bodies, helpers, exports, and unrelated files in both source layouts.

tasks.title: Generate readable acceptance-test bodies
tasks.hypothesis: Typed, ordered examples can generate tests expressed entirely through domain operations.
tests: Generate the four readable shopping calls from the agreed example.
Preserve different initial states and action order.
Produce equivalent tests from inline and separate examples.

tasks.title: Generate reusable domain-operation interfaces and scaffolds
tasks.hypothesis: Declared actions and observations can become reusable typed helpers beneath generated tests.
tests: Reuse one operation across several scenarios.
Reject an undeclared operation.
Generate an explicit unfinished body for a declared operation without implementation.

tasks.title: Generate assertions from observations and input/output examples
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit predicates can produce working checks that compare observed behavior with independently specified expectations.
tests: Generate an equality assertion for the example multiply(8, 8) => 64.
Check the application's actual basket quantity rather than test-side call counts.
Fail when an observation returns the wrong value or remains unimplemented.

tasks.title: Implement reusable setup, scenario context, and helper composition
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit defaults and compositions can fill in repetitive setup without hiding unspecified assumptions.
tests: Share declared fixture setup across scenarios.
Pass context and results between composed operations.
Keep scenarios isolated from one another.

tasks.title: Connect domain operations to project drivers and public interfaces
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit execution mappings can connect readable tests to a real system without embedding transport details in those tests.
tests: Run a domain operation through a handwritten or dependency-supplied driver.
Generate a supported driver when the specification supplies the required details.
Preserve driver implementations across regeneration.

tasks.title: Track prose expectations and incomplete executable work
tasks.hypothesis: Preserving descriptive requirements as visible obligations lets authors specify behavior before its verification is fully defined.
tests: Retain a prose expectation that lacks an executable observation.
Distinguish invalid source, unfinished implementation, and verified behavior.
Attach a later executable check without losing the original requirement.

tasks.title: Implement mapped contract and expectation updates
tasks.hypothesis: update can revise mapped structure and behavioral obligations while retaining handwritten implementations.
tests: Change a supported signature or field while preserving unrelated source.
Change saving from local storage to Supabase without rewriting the existing save body.
Report newly unfinished implementation work and invalidate evidence for the replaced expectation.

tasks.title: Implement mapped renames and moves
tasks.hypothesis: Established identity mappings can carry existing implementations through supported renames and file moves.
tests: Rename a capability between two valid specifications while retaining its body.
Move a concept between files without losing associated handwritten content.
Update supported structural references and report remaining affected references under the chosen preservation policy.

tasks.title: Implement removals with handwritten-code retention
tasks.hypothesis: delete can remove supported generated structure while keeping handwritten work available when removal is unresolved.
tests: Remove an unused generated element that contains no handwritten work.
Report a conflict and retain an implementation when no retention decision exists.
Apply an explicitly established retention or migration decision and expose affected consumers.

tasks.title: Reconcile repeated builds and record versioned outcomes
tasks.hypothesis: Recording actual applied changes and their inputs can make repeated builds stable and subsequent learning traceable.
tests: Repeat an unchanged build without additional source edits.
Record the manifest version, relevant build inputs, applied changes, and outstanding obligations.
Keep failed or partial builds distinct from successful baselines and avoid reusing evidence for changed requirements.

tasks.title: Implement UML structure and dependency output
tasks.hypothesis: A diagram output can render declared concepts, contracts, and relationships from the shared model.
tests: Render concepts, public capabilities, and types.
Show the declared dependency and structural relationships.
Keep the diagram consistent with the code contract.

tasks.title: Implement UML interaction and sequence output
tasks.hypothesis: Explicit messages and their order can become an interaction diagram without guessing behavior from dependencies.
tests: Render a specified StoreGame-to-Storage message sequence.
Use the same declared order as the scenario/documentation.
Report missing sequence information for a dependency-only input.

tasks.title: Implement Markdown specification output
tasks.hypothesis: A documentation output can make the same contracts and examples readable without maintaining a separate manual specification.
tests: Render contracts, dependencies, scenarios, and implementation obligations.
Update documentation when the specification changes.
Preserve handwritten documentation included in the connected output.

tasks.title: Connect validation, generation, and project updates into one build
tasks.hypothesis: One build operation can resolve the specification, choose configured outputs, and coordinate their changes in the connected project.
tests: Build a valid contract into its selected project and targets.
Reject invalid input before output is applied.
Return actual changes, conflicts, and unfinished work.

tasks.title: Write the compiler's first usable self-description
tasks.hypothesis: Expressing the compiler's own contracts and acceptance examples will expose language-design gaps while producing useful development artifacts.
tests: Describe validation, generation, the output API, and their supporting types in .expec.
Trace generated checks back to the compiler's stories.
Identify which parts still require the handwritten bootstrap tool.

tasks.title: Generate and evolve the compiler through its own specifications
tasks.hypothesis: A working bootstrap compiler can generate its own contracts and tests, then maintain them as the tool evolves.
tests: Generate selected compiler artifacts from the self-description and connect their implementations.
Change a compiler contract and regenerate while preserving its implementation.
Reproduce the selected artifacts with the newly built tool.

tasks.title: Implement the Store Game pilot and record requirement feedback
tasks.hypothesis: Building and changing a real connected project will show whether .expec meets the original needs and which proposed solutions need revision.
tests: Take Store Game from specification through scaffolding, working tests, and implementation.
Revise a contract, inspect project differences, regenerate, and verify the corrected behavior.
Record observed results and unresolved gaps against the affected stories and pitches.

tasks.title: Implement Kotlin project inspection and editing
tasks.hypothesis: Kotlin-specific source support can preserve handwritten Kotlin code under the shared read, search, and change contracts.
tests: Read a complete concept and find its Kotlin references.
Apply a structural fixture change without losing its implementation.
Report unsupported constructs and ambiguous mappings.

tasks.title: Implement the Kotlin output adapter
tasks.hypothesis: The shared model can generate equivalent Kotlin contracts and supported executable specifications through target-specific mappings.
tests: Generate the agreed contract and scenario fixtures in Kotlin.
Preserve Kotlin implementations during a supported structural change.
Report source concepts outside the adapter's supported mappings.

tasks.title: Implement Java project inspection and editing
tasks.hypothesis: Java-specific source support can preserve handwritten Java code under the shared read, search, and change contracts.
tests: Read a complete concept and find its Java references.
Apply a structural fixture change without losing its implementation.
Report unsupported constructs and ambiguous mappings.

tasks.title: Implement the Java output adapter
tasks.hypothesis: Java can use the same resolved specification while expressing contracts and test support through its own language conventions.
tests: Generate the agreed contract and scenario fixtures in Java.
Preserve Java implementations during a supported structural change.
Report unsupported mappings explicitly.

tasks.title: Implement Python project inspection and editing
tasks.hypothesis: Python-specific source support can preserve handwritten Python code while making limits on dynamic reference discovery explicit.
tests: Read a complete concept and find its resolvable Python uses.
Apply a structural fixture change without losing its implementation.
Disclose unresolved dynamic uses rather than claiming absence.

tasks.title: Implement the Python output adapter
tasks.hypothesis: The model can preserve contract meaning in Python without requiring every concept to map to a statically typed class.
tests: Generate the agreed contract and scenario fixtures in Python.
Preserve Python implementations during a supported structural change.
Make target-specific limitations visible.

tasks.title: Publish an exporter development kit and conformance examples
tasks.hypothesis: A documented API, minimal adapter example, and shared contract checks let another developer add a useful output independently.
tests: Build and register a small additional output using the published API.
Run shared API checks, including supported read and search responsibilities.
Demonstrate unsupported-feature reporting without changing the parser.

tasks.title: Package the tool and write the first project walkthrough
tasks.hypothesis: A versioned tool package and a short walkthrough will let an author initialize, validate, build, and revise a project without repository internals.
tests: Run the packaged tool in a clean fixture environment.
Follow the manifest and build walkthrough on Store Game.
Document adding an output and resolving common diagnostics.
